clue.text: An expert entertained in large country house made merry

indicators.note: being entertained in a house means being held inside it, so these letters go within the house

parts.note: a hall is a big manor house in the country
an is the indefinite article, A
a dab, or dab hand, is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist is a guest at a stately home, and the evening turns festive.
explanation.walkthrough: DAB, as in dab hand, is British slang for someone skilled.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to have enjoyed oneself enormously is to have celebrated, as a merrymaker does.

clue.text: Hard course set up needing everyone to finish book

indicators.note: says the next piece comes at the end of the answer
in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised so they read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a flow is a course or current of water
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A tough curriculum is arranged, and everyone has to get through a set text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns the first two pieces round to give WOLFH, since this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilary Mantel's Booker-winning novel about Thomas Cromwell carries this title, so it is a book.

clue.text: A little drink for each little child

parts.note: a nip is a small measure of spirits
per means for each, as in per head

explanation.surface: A tot of spirits handed round, one per small child, sounds like a dubious party.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial synonym: a youngster or small kid is affectionately called by this informal name in British speech.

clue.text: Business arrangement that's dealt with by letter

definitions.text: Business arrangement that's dealt with by letter

parts.words: Business arrangement that's dealt with by letter
parts.note: a letter here is not correspondence but one who lets property, a landlord, who handles this kind of rental deal

explanation.surface: A commercial deal conducted entirely through the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' reads as written correspondence, but it means one who lets, a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A rental agreement under which someone occupies property is arranged by the landlord, the one who lets it.

clue.text: In America, unfairly, Hillary's No 1 female monster

indicators.note: In places the first letter of the name inside the rearranged country letters
unfairly suggests something treated wrongly, so the letters of the country are jumbled
Hillary's number one is the first letter of that name

explanation.surface: A politician's opponents paint Hillary as a monstrous woman, treated unfairly in American politics.
explanation.walkthrough: AMERICA rearranged as CIMAERA takes H inside after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the fire-breathing beast with lion, goat and serpent parts was female.

clue.text: Drug must hurt terribly — hesitation involved

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up inside, so the hesitation goes into the rearranged letters
terribly signals the letters of must hurt are jumbled

parts.note: er is the sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.surface: A medicine that stings badly, given after a moment's hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges MUST HURT as TRUTHSUM; 'involved' puts ER inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug supposedly forcing a person to speak honestly under interrogation, such as sodium pentothal.

clue.text: My group getting back support?

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A band member wonders whether the group is backing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is an exclamation, not a possessive; COR is the British equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff undergarment shapes and braces the torso, so it can serve to support a spine; the question mark flags this loose reading.

clue.text: A number err, backsliding in church, put on a holy pedestal?

indicators.note: in places the pieces within the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: backsliding means going backwards, so the word for err reads in reverse

parts.note: to err is to sin

explanation.surface: A number of churchgoers who stray morally, yet someone is still idolised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backsliding' reverses the sin; CE, the Church of England, is the commonest crossword church.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare someone a saint officially elevates them to venerated status, a literal holy pedestal.

clue.text: Loose woman cut short by wife in Essex town

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a harlot is a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: A disreputable woman is snubbed by a married woman in a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: HARLOT less its last letter is HARLO; Essex is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A new town in the English county of Essex, built after the Second World War.

clue.text: Time of semi-revolution

parts.note: a revolution is a full turn of the clock's minute hand, so going halfway round takes thirty minutes

explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-revolution' hints at a partial political uprising, but it is the minute hand going halfway round.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirty minutes is the interval in which a clock's minute hand completes half its circuit.

clue.text: Premier receiving taunt ("dull"!) is following course of what's possible

indicators.note: receiving means taking the pieces inside

parts.note: PM stands for Prime Minister, the premier
to rag is to tease or taunt
mat, or matt, means dull, without shine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prime minister, mocked as boring, settles for what can actually be achieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dull' in brackets and quotes reads as the taunt itself, but it is a separate piece, matt spelt with one T.
explanation.definitionFit: A philosophy of practicality: dealing with things sensibly and realistically rather than idealistically.

clue.text: Stone container holding food knocked over

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the reversed food goes within

parts.note: a jar is a container

indicators.note: knocked over means turned upside down, reading backwards here

parts.note: an egg is food

explanation.surface: A jar holding food is knocked over, perhaps by a thrown stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns EGG into GGE; Stone means a member of the Rolling Stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Mick, the lead singer of the Rolling Stones, is the most famous member of that band.

clue.text: Doubling of development not right

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for right is removed

parts.note: germination is the development of a seed

explanation.surface: A dull report on how a project doubled, but without the correct development.
explanation.walkthrough: GERMINATION loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical term, from the Latin for twin, for the duplication of a consonant or other element.

clue.text: Black liquid, supplied by Native American, old drunk swallowed

indicators.note: swallowed means taken inside, so the pieces go within the people

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
a sot is a drunk

explanation.surface: An elderly alcoholic gulps down some dark fluid offered by a Native American.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark oily tar distillate is painted on fences to preserve the wood.

clue.text: Defect sees bishop giving way to strong language

indicators.note: giving way to means one letter yields its place to another

parts.note: a blemish is a defect
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
F stands for forte, strong, in music

explanation.surface: A cleric who swears, and it is seen as a flaw.
explanation.walkthrough: In BLEMISH, B makes way for F; 'strong language' looks like swearing, but the definition is just 'language'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch variety spoken in Flanders, northern Belgium, is a recognised tongue.

clue.text: Turn up for palmist set up in seat specially

indicators.note: specially means arranged for a particular purpose, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller turns up, and a seat is specially arranged for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is a link; 'specially' rearranges UP IN SEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate the hand so the palm faces upward, exactly what a reader of hands asks a client to do.

clue.text: Fabric items, manufactured stuff for Germany

indicators.note: for means one piece takes the place of another

parts.note: made means manufactured
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
to cram is to stuff

explanation.surface: A textile shop's goods: fabric made in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: In MADE, CRAM replaces D, the letter for Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotted cord work used for wall hangings and plant holders produces textile objects.

clue.text: Rodent with 'orrible smell climbing fruit plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards

parts.note: the dropped h of 'orrible says to drop it from hum, a smell, too, leaving um
a squash is a plant bearing gourd fruits

explanation.surface: A rat clambering up a vine with a nasty stink.
explanation.walkthrough: HUM is British slang for a bad smell; the Cockney 'orrible drops its H, giving UM, and 'climbing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the muskrat, a North American aquatic gnawing mammal.

clue.text: Hold back stalwart

definitions.meaning: to stem a flow, as of blood

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, a variant of stanch, stopping bleeding; as an adjective, firmly loyal.

clue.text: Baddie offering liquid drug on street

indicators.note: on means the following pieces sit after, as if placed upon, the street

parts.note: ink is a liquid
pot is cannabis

explanation.surface: A villain peddling a liquid narcotic on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in an across clue means the street comes first and the rest is laid after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang insult for a contemptible, unpleasant person, a villain.

clue.text: RIP in place, erected when member is buried

indicators.note: buried means placed inside, so the organ goes within
in a down clue, erected means raised to read upwards

parts.note: to put is to place
an ear is a part, or member, of the body

explanation.surface: An inscription set up where a body part is buried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns PUT into TUP; 'is buried' puts EAR inside. RIP looks like the gravestone abbreviation but is the verb to tear.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip something is to tear it into pieces, as with a contract.

clue.text: Careless soldiers fail to hit target

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
to miss is to fail to hit

explanation.surface: Sloppy troops keep missing what they aim at.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers is a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: negligent, failing in one's duty.

clue.text: Guy not allowed richly seasoned food

parts.note: to guy is to mock or tease, as is to rag
out means not allowed, as in that idea is out

explanation.surface: A man is barred from eating spicy fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man but is the verb to ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly flavoured French stew of meat and vegetables.

clue.text: Cake having a piece of wood? Food sent back

parts.note: a batten is a strip of wood

indicators.note: food that is sent back in a restaurant is returned, so the word for food is read in the return direction

parts.note: grub is food

explanation.surface: A diner returns a cake with a bit of timber in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses GRUB to BURG.
explanation.definitionFit: A chequered pink and yellow sponge wrapped in marzipan, a British teatime classic.

clue.text: See 10
See 2
Objection when second person gets involved in business deal

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside, so the pronoun goes within the objection

parts.note: a but is an objection, as in no buts
you is the second-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A protest when a second party muscles into a company transaction.
explanation.definitionFit: A purchase of a controlling share in a company is a corporate transaction.

clue.text: Not exactly precipitate, is husband rude?

parts.note: c, for circa, means about, not exactly
to precipitate is to throw down, hurl
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wife wonders whether her husband is impolite, not exactly hasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precipitate' looks like rain or haste but means to fling.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: boorish and surly, ill-mannered.
